text: Small, uncooked, unpressed curds drained in individual moulds give a soft, slightly chalky little cheese that is eaten within days and tastes sweetly of milk. If it is kept longer, a Geotrichum bloom softens the chalky core.

steps.note: Whole cow milk, raw in the past.
To hazelnut size, and not cooked.
Ladled into small plastic moulds 10 cm across and drained, with optional Geotrichum candidum spores.
Dry-salted or brined during the draining.
Turned daily in cold rooms, and a light white Geotrichum bloom grows if it is kept longer.
